sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Sector leadership remains highly concentrated in Energy and Technology, while Healthcare suffered a sharp near-term drop and defensives continue to lag.

Energy and Technology are the market's clear anchors, representing the only 2 of 11 sectors exhibiting all-green performance across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD timeframes. Energy in particular displays sustained, dominant strength as the undisputed top performer, holding the rank 1 spot with a market-leading 0.967 momentum score. 

Rotational flows over the past five sessions favored cyclicals and value-oriented segments, with Financials, Industrials, and Real Estate each advancing 1 spot. In contrast, Healthcare saw the steepest deterioration across the board, tumbling 3 spots to rank 7. Broad momentum laggards remain clustered in rate-sensitive and consumer groups, anchored by Consumer Cyclical and Utilities at the bottom of the rankings.

## Strength
- **Narrow all-green breadth:** Only 2 of 11 sectors—Energy (momentum 0.967) and Technology (momentum 0.850)—are positive across all trailing periods (week, month, quarter, half, and YTD).
- **Persistent leadership:** Energy is the sole group demonstrating sustained strength, holding a top-3 rank across 1-month, 3-month, and 6-month horizons while maintaining the rank 1 spot YTD.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Five-session rank gainers:** Financials (+1 to rank 5, momentum 0.650), Industrials (+1 to rank 4, momentum 0.417), and Real Estate (+1 to rank 6, momentum 0.333) showed the largest short-term improvements.
- **Sharp pullback in Healthcare:** Healthcare fell 3 spots over the last 5 sessions to rank 7, despite holding a mid-tier momentum score of 0.52.
- **Deepest momentum laggards:** Consumer Cyclical (rank 11, momentum 0.150) and Utilities (rank 10, momentum 0.183) remain the weakest groups in the market, followed by Consumer Defensive (rank 8, momentum 0.300).

## Divergences
- **Communication Services rank vs. momentum:** Communication Services holds an above-median momentum score of 0.567 (tied with Basic Materials) despite a depressed YTD rank of 9.
- **Industrials short-term push vs. weak baseline:** Industrials gained 1 spot over 5 sessions to reach rank 4, yet carries an overall sub-50 momentum score of 0.417.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy and tech hardware dominate market leadership with exceptionally high momentum, while healthcare segments show sharp short-term distribution.

Energy and hardware supply chains remain the strongest areas of the market, led by Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.984 momentum) and Computer Hardware (0.927 momentum). Overall breadth is narrow, with only 9 of 144 groups holding all-green status across all timeframes. Consumer Electronics continues to accelerate into leadership, gaining 11 spots to reach rank 30 alongside an 0.883 momentum score.

Rotation is hitting healthcare and select commodities. Medical Care Facilities posted the session's largest rank jump (+15 spots to rank 63), but neighboring segments like Health Information Services (-21 spots) and Drug Manufacturers - General (-11 spots) dropped rapidly. Consumer discretionary laggards continue to anchor the bottom of the market, with Footwear & Accessories (0.058 momentum) and Recreational Vehicles (0.155 momentum) showing persistent multi-month weakness.

## Strength
- **Narrow leadership footprint:** Only 9 of 144 industry groups are all-green across week, month, quarter, half, and YTD windows.
- **Energy leadership:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing leads the entire market with an 0.984 momentum score (YTD rank 2), supported by Oil & Gas Integrated (0.88 momentum) and Oil & Gas E&P (0.82 momentum).
- **Tech hardware & shipping dominance:** Sustained top-tier ranks across 1, 3, and 6 months are anchored by Marine Shipping (0.946 momentum), Electronics & Computer Distribution (0.935 momentum), and Computer Hardware (0.927 momentum).

## Movers & Momentum
- **Fastest short-term gainers:** Medical Care Facilities led 5-day rank improvement (+15 to rank 63, momentum 0.71), followed by Confectioners (+14 to rank 52) and Insurance - Diversified (+14 to rank 79).
- **Sharpest 5-day drops:** Health Information Services experienced the largest decline, shedding 21 spots to rank 51, while Auto & Truck Dealerships (-14 to rank 122) and Uranium (-14 to rank 89) also sold off aggressively.
- **Deepest momentum laggards:** Footwear & Accessories (0.058 momentum, YTD rank 141), Mortgage Finance (0.129 momentum, YTD rank 142), and Airports & Air Services (0.131 momentum, YTD rank 140) remain the weakest performers.

## Divergences
- **Fading momentum leaders:** Several high-momentum industries are experiencing sudden rank erosion, led by Health Information Services (0.64 momentum; -21 spots in 5 sessions), Coking Coal (0.64 momentum; -13 spots), Silver (0.64 momentum; -9 spots), and Biotechnology (0.72 momentum; -8 spots).
- **Emerging early-stage movers:** Industrials and defensives are improving in rank despite weak underlying momentum, including Airlines (+8 spots, 0.44 momentum), Aerospace & Defense (+7 spots, 0.36 momentum), and Grocery Stores (+7 spots, 0.30 momentum).
